chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Dawud, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a man vomits while he is in a state of purity, let him rinse his mouth.
ai.seo_question: Does vomiting break wudu in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies a key distinction in Shia fiqh: vomiting does not nullify wudu, unlike in some other schools of thought, reflecting the principle that minor impurities do not break ritual purity. The requirement to rinse the mouth (mutammad) serves as a corrective measure for residual taste or impurity rather than a full renewal of the ablution state. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on ease in worship while maintaining physical cleanliness.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Abu Dawood, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat, from Aban, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
When the man vomits and he is upon purity, so let him rinse his mouth’.
en.sarwar: 10. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and abu Dawud from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Aban from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one vomits while his Wudu’ is valid, he should only rinse his mouth.’”
